clue.text: Exclusive command of the game

definitions.meaning: sole control of a market, with no competitor allowed
the board game of buying streets and building hotels

explanation.surface: Someone has total control of a game night.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is sole control of a trade; the other is the property-trading board game.

clue.text: Unintentionally exceeded the limit

parts.note: describes going past a target by accident, as a pilot does with a runway or a shooter with a mark

explanation.surface: Someone went too far without meaning to.
explanation.definitionFit: To go past a mark or runway end by mistake is the meaning.

clue.text: Getting into deep water?

parts.note: the idiom for getting into trouble, read instead as a ship heading out to sea

explanation.surface: Someone is getting into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel leaving harbour for the open sea is described this way; it is also an adventure-training charity name.

clue.text: Great numbers of dogs losing their heads

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: poodles are a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Many dogs are decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing their heads' drops the first letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots or heaps, a colloquial word for a large quantity.

clue.text: It has its ups and downs as a plaything

definitions.text: It has its ups and downs as a plaything

parts.words: It has its ups and downs as a plaything
parts.note: describes a spinning toy that climbs and falls on a string, while hinting at a life of mixed fortune

explanation.surface: Something that goes through good times and bad, like a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool toy on a string rises and falls repeatedly.

clue.text: City still on cloud nine

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
static means motionless

explanation.surface: The city stays calm and blissful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on cloud nine is an idiom for being overjoyed.

clue.text: Acknowledge a promise

parts.note: a vow is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to having made a pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare or admit openly is to acknowledge.

clue.text: Ray eager to resolve doubtful situation

indicators.note: to resolve here is to break down and rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ray is keen to settle an uncertain matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ill-defined matter, neither clearly one thing nor another, is an unclear case.

clue.text: A survey not repeated

definitions.meaning: done a single time and then finished

explanation.surface: A survey that will not be carried out again.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick look is a brief inspection; read literally the phrase says something happened a single time and is finished.

clue.text: Being out of step he annoys one

indicators.note: being out of order or out of line signals the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who marches out of step irritates the rest of the squad.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is someone who irritates others.

clue.text: Far into a journey for a thirsty traveller?

definitions.meaning: making good progress, a long way along
a source of water found along the route would suit someone parched

explanation.surface: A thirsty traveller has made good progress on a long journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means progressing nicely; taken literally it is a water source beside the road.

clue.text: Inflation? Cut rising going rate perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to axe is to cut

indicators.note: perhaps signals one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Economic inflation might be cured by cutting the going rate.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags inflation in the sense of puffing a story up, not rising prices, which the surface about the going rate pushes you towards.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflating a story means overstating it.

clue.text: Quietly he accepts a pay increase, the hypocrite

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly

indicators.note: one word taking in other letters signals a container

parts.note: taken as written
a rise is a raise in wages

explanation.surface: A two-faced man quietly takes a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts ARISE inside HE, giving HARISEE after P.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees are the sect condemned as hypocrites in the Gospels, so the name stands for a sanctimonious person.

clue.text: Terminal heart trouble?

indicators.note: trouble suggests stirring things up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A fatal heart condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' suggests fatal, but it is an electrical terminal, the ground connection.
explanation.definitionFit: In wiring, the ground connection is a terminal on a plug.

clue.text: Revolutionary painting returned by dealer

indicators.note: something returned is sent back, so the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: red is the colour of revolutionaries
art is painting and similar work

explanation.surface: A dealer sends back a revolutionary painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant who buys and sells goods is a dealer.

clue.text: Drive point home in an essay

definitions.meaning: thrust a sharp point into something
an essay is an attempt, as in 'have a go'

explanation.surface: An essay writer pushes their argument hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To jab with a blade is to thrust; 'essay' in its old sense is an attempt, as is 'having a go'.

clue.text: Entitles constituents to make themselves at home

indicators.note: constituents are the component parts, which are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Voters are given the right to feel comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: To become comfortable in a new place is to get settled.

clue.text: Maurice has a heart of gold

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so its outer letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Maurice is a kind man with a heart of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means made of or containing gold, from the Latin aurum.

clue.text: A Greek writes one article, then I write another

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
taken as written
taken as written
an is another indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Greek author writes one piece and then another.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Athens is a Greek.

clue.text: A stage joke turned fatuous with the passage of time

definitions.text: fatuous with the passage of time

indicators.note: turned round signals the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a gag is a comedian's joke

explanation.surface: A comic's joke goes sour and silly as the years pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' turns AGAG round, which still reads the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Senile or doting in old age is a slang sense of the word.

clue.text: Get blooming old?

parts.note: flowering plants left too long run to flowers and pods, and the phrase also describes a person declining

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about getting jolly old.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that bolt into flower stop being useful; figuratively a person lets themselves deteriorate.

clue.text: Depression pigs get into

definitions.meaning: a low point, as in an economic or weather dip
pigs climb into their feeding container

explanation.surface: Pigs take refuge in a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow or low point is a depression; a farm feeding container is where pigs eat.

clue.text: There's a lot of laughter when a girl swallows it

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: Hilary is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everyone laughs when a girl gulps something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' and 'when' are link words; the girl's name is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Great merriment or loud amusement is the meaning.

clue.text: Awkward ordeal for one putting on weight

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Gaining weight is an uncomfortable trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting on weight' suggests getting fat, but it means stowing heavy goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who places cargo aboard a vehicle carries out the work of filling it.

clue.text: Bringing down a plane in action on d-day

definitions.meaning: the skill of touching an aircraft down safely
vessels used to put troops ashore in the Normandy invasion of 1944

explanation.surface: A plane is brought down during the D-Day fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it is the art of touching down; as a phrase it names the boats that put troops on the beaches.

clue.text: What thieves do in prison

definitions.meaning: slang for a jail or police station

explanation.surface: Thieves do their stealing while locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for stealing and for a jail.

clue.text: Potting aids

parts.note: potting is sinking balls in snooker or pool, not gardening

explanation.definitionFit: Sticks used to strike balls into pockets in snooker.

clue.text: Perfect but inconclusive thought

indicators.note: without a conclusion, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A perfect thought that leads nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or plan formed in the mind is a thought.

clue.text: Extra fashionable line in trousers

parts.note: in means in fashion
a crease is the pressed fold down trouser legs

explanation.surface: A trendy extra crease pressed into trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition or rise, something extra, is a growth in amount.

clue.text: Song composed by Edna Rees

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of the names are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Edna Rees has written a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A love song sung beneath a window is the classic example of this kind of piece.
